1860.content: How OrkStage runs OpenTofu in throwaway containers, keeps one S3 state per resource without secrets, plans before apply and scans for drift.

1868.content:
OrkStage provisions AWS with OpenTofu modules in `infra/tofu/modules/aws/*`, one module per logical
resource type.
ADR 0005 records the
design.

1869.content:
The worker never runs OpenTofu in its own process. Every `tofu` command runs in a **throwaway
container**: the pinned `ghcr.io/opentofu/opentofu:1.12.7` image, or the `tofu-runner` image with
the modules baked in.

1870.content:
The module library is mounted read only, or baked into the image. Providers come from a plugin
cache volume that all runners share.

1871.content:
Credentials reach **that one container only**, as environment variables. They never appear in
files, command lines or state.

1872.content: Each command has a hard timeout (`TOFU_TIMEOUT_MINUTES`, 45 by default) and can be cancelled.

1873.content:
Today the worker starts runners through the Docker socket, which gives it control of the host's
Docker daemon. A runner that uses ECS RunTask or a Kubernetes Job with a scoped role is on the
roadmap.

1874.content:
The state key is `orkstage/<physical-name>.tfstate`. There is one state for each resource, not one
for each instance or placement slot. This design:

1875.content: keeps the platform's own DAG, with progress, retries and failure isolation for each resource;

1876.content: limits the damage of a broken state file to one resource;

1877.content:
passes dependencies as module outputs that become inputs of the next module. Every module emits a
`kind` output, so the adapter wires them by type;

1878.content:
stores the exact root configuration next to the state (`.config.json`), so a destroy never depends
on a template that has changed since.

1879.content:
**Backend**: S3, with `use_lockfile` for locking, and encryption. On real AWS, you create the bucket
in advance with versioning and encryption, and OrkStage validates it before use (see
Connecting an AWS account). On an
emulator, OrkStage creates the bucket on first use.

1880.content:
An OpenTofu `ephemeral` resource generates each RDS master password, and the module writes it
through write only attributes (`password_wo`, `secret_string_wo`). Services receive the ARN of the
Secrets Manager secret as an ECS secret. We verified that the state holds `password: null`.

1881.content:
In the **Generate plan** phase, the worker runs a real `tofu plan` for every **existing** resource
whose desired state changed. It writes a summary for each resource to the deployment's event log:

1882.content:
A deletion or replacement makes the deployment **high risk**. A routine new revision of an ECS task
definition (for a new image digest) does not.

1883.content:
For a `production` instance, high risk **escalates** the deployment to `AWAITING_APPROVAL`, even
when the platform's own diff predicted only an update.

1884.content: When no change is destructive, the approval step is marked skipped, with the reason.

1885.content: The deployment stores the provider plans (`plan.providerPlans`) for review.

1886.content:
Every `DRIFT_CHECK_INTERVAL_MINUTES` (360 by default, `0` turns scans off), the worker plans each
applied resource on real providers again, from the snapshot it was deployed with. Any planned action
means someone changed the resource outside OrkStage. The resource then becomes `DRIFT_DETECTED`,
OrkStage writes an audit event and sends `instance.drift_detected`. The scan skips resources with
pending changes. A new deployment restores the configuration from the template.

1887.content:
When someone deletes a resource outside OrkStage, its recorded state outlives it. The AWS adapter
has a **live existence probe** for this case:

1888.content:
During **verification**, OrkStage probes any resource that is not healthy. If the resource no
longer exists, the step fails at once with
`Resource no longer exists at the provider. Redeploy to re-create it.` instead of waiting.

1889.content:
Verification waits in **one settle window of 5 minutes per deployment**, not one per resource, so a
slow service does not multiply the wait.

1890.content:
On the **next deployment**, the executor asks the provider whether converged resources still exist.
It recreates the missing ones instead of skipping them as unchanged.

1891.content:
The AWS adapter has been tested end to end against MiniStack with: VPC, subnets and security groups,
ECR, SQS with a dead letter queue, S3, Secrets Manager, RDS Postgres (real container), an ElastiCache
Valkey replication group (real container), an ALB with target groups and listener rules (live data
plane at `/_alb/<name>/`), an ECS Fargate service (real container, registered in the target group and
healthy), Route 53 and ACM. The adapter contract suite passes against it.

1893.content: OrkStage stores references to secrets, not values. The env and AWS Secrets Manager schemes, JSON keys, emulator settings and where each secret lives.

1896.content: Other secrets and where they live

1898.content:
OrkStage stores **references** to secrets, never their values, and resolves each reference at the
moment it is used. Values are not written to the database, not returned by the API and not logged.

1899.content:
| Reference    | Resolved from                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `env://NAME` | An environment variable of the API and worker processes. `NAME` contains uppercase letters, digits and `_`. Suits local development and simple installations. |

1900.content:
| Reference                | Resolved from                                        |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `aws-sm://<name-or-arn>` | The `SecretString` of an AWS Secrets Manager secret. |

1901.content:
| Reference                          | Resolved from                                 |
| ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `aws-sm://<name-or-arn>#<jsonKey>` | One string field of a secret that holds JSON. |

1902.content:
The `credentialRef` of a cloud target must use one of these schemes. The API rejects anything else,
including a pasted secret value.

1903.content:
OrkStage reads `aws-sm://` secrets with the **control plane's own AWS credentials**, found through the
default provider chain (ECS task role, EC2 instance profile, SSO or environment). It does not use a
customer's deployment role for this.

1904.content:
| Setting              | Default     | Meaning                                                           |
| -------------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SECRETS_AWS_REGION` | `us-east-1` | Region for references given by name. ARNs carry their own region. |

1905.content:
| Setting                | Default | Meaning                                                                                 |
| ---------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SECRETS_AWS_ENDPOINT` |         | Endpoint override for emulators such as MiniStack, as seen from the API and the worker. |

1906.content:
The control plane identity needs `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue` on the referenced secrets, and
`kms:Decrypt` when a secret uses a customer managed KMS key.

1907.content:
Values are cached in memory for five minutes, so a deployment with many references does not hit
Secrets Manager rate limits. Error messages show the secret name in redacted form and keep only the
error class, because AWS SDK messages can include account ids.

1908.content:
| Secret                                                                          | Where it lives                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SESSION_SECRET`, `ENCRYPTION_KEY`, `ORKSTAGE_LICENSE_KEY`, OIDC client secrets | Environment of the API and the worker. Inject them from your secret store. |

1909.content:
| Secret                                             | Where it lives                                                                  |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Webhook signing secrets (they start with `whsec_`) | Database, encrypted with `ENCRYPTION_KEY`. Shown once, when created or rotated. |

1910.content:
| Secret         | Where it lives                                               |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| API key tokens | Only their SHA-256 hash is stored. Shown once, when created. |

1911.content:
| Secret                                          | Where it lives                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Database passwords of provisioned RDS instances | OpenTofu generates them as ephemeral values and passes them through write only attributes to RDS and to a Secrets Manager secret in the customer account. **The state holds `password: null`.** Services receive the secret's ARN. |

1912.content:
| Secret                                | Where it lives                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| AWS credentials for customer accounts | Never stored. Short lived AssumeRole credentials stay in memory and reach one runner container as environment variables. |

1913.content:
Resolvers for other secret stores (Azure Key Vault, OCI Vault, HashiCorp Vault) will arrive with the
matching provider adapters.

1915.content: Security controls built into OrkStage, a hardening checklist for hosting it yourself, the known gaps and how to report a vulnerability.

1920.content:
| Area     | Control                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Sessions | An opaque random token of 32 bytes in an `httpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax` cookie (`Secure` in production). Only its SHA-256 hash is stored. Sessions expire after 12 hours and are revoked on logout. |

1921.content:
| Area | Control                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| CSRF | Every request with a session that changes state must send `x-orkstage-csrf: 1`. The API allows no CORS from other origins, so a browser on another site cannot send this header. Requests with a bearer API key are exempt. |

1922.content:
| Area | Control                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ---- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| OIDC | Authorization code grant with PKCE (S256). `state` and `nonce` are verified. The flow state lives in a signed, short lived cookie. `returnTo` accepts relative paths only. Provider tokens are discarded. |

1923.content:
| Area            | Control                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Account linking | Only through an email address the provider has verified (`email_verified`, or `xms_edov` for Entra). OrkStage never trusts `preferred_username`, which prevents takeover in the style of "nOAuth". Unknown users get no account unless a tenant has put their domain on its allowlist. |

1924.content:
| Area      | Control                                                                                          |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Dev login | Off unless `AUTH_DEV_LOGIN_ENABLED=true`. Startup fails if it is on while `NODE_ENV=production`. |

1925.content:
| Area     | Control                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| API keys | Only the SHA-256 hash of the token is stored. Scopes narrow a role and never exceed it. A key cannot manage keys. Keys support expiry, revocation and a last used time. Every action is audited with the key's name and prefix. |

1926.content:
| Area          | Control                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Authorization | CASL abilities for each request. Queries for tenant data are scoped to the caller's memberships, and each record is checked again after loading. Records of other tenants return 404, not 403. |

1927.content:
| Area    | Control                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Secrets | The API rejects target configuration with keys that look like secrets. Credentials are `env://` or `aws-sm://` references. Services receive secret references, not values. |

1928.content:
| Area              | Control                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Cloud credentials | AssumeRole with an external id. The credentials are short lived, stay in memory and reach only the runner container that needs them. |

1929.content:
| Area     | Control                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Webhooks | HMAC-SHA256 signatures with a timestamp, and `https` only. SSRF protection blocks private, loopback, link local and multicast targets, checked at registration and again before each delivery. No redirects are followed, the timeout is 10 seconds, and signing secrets are encrypted at rest. |

1930.content:
| Area    | Control                                                                                                                          |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Logging | Pino redacts tokens, secrets, cookies and authorization headers. Errors return a code and a correlation id, never a stack trace. |

1931.content:
| Area        | Control                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Rate limits | 600 requests per minute per client overall. Stricter limits apply to login, deploy, destroy, target validation, template publishing, API key creation, imports and webhook tests. |

1932.content:
| Area  | Control                                                                           |
| ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Audit | Append only. A Postgres trigger rejects `UPDATE` and `DELETE` on the audit table. |

1933.content:
| Area    | Control                                            |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Headers | Helmet with a restrictive Content Security Policy. |

1934.content:
| Area         | Control                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Supply chain | Only pnpm build scripts on an allowlist run. Telemetry during install is denied. Very recent releases are avoided (minimum release age). Container images are pinned by digest where it matters (MiniStack, OpenTofu). |

1937.content:
TLS in front of the console and the API, with `WEB_PUBLIC_URL` and `API_PUBLIC_URL` on
    `https://`.

1938.content: Postgres and Redis on private networks, with authentication and encryption in transit.

1939.content:
The worker on a dedicated host (it holds the Docker socket), with an IAM identity limited to
    `sts:AssumeRole` on your `orkstage-deploy` roles and `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue` on the
    referenced secrets.

1940.content:
One AWS account per environment, with deployment roles created from the provided
    CloudFormation template and a unique external id for each.

1941.content: State buckets versioned, encrypted and private.

1943.content: One API key per integration, with the smallest preset and an expiry.

1944.content: Postgres backups tested by restoring them (see Backups and recovery).

1945.content: MFA policy, and a console page that lists and revokes sessions.

1946.content: Container image scanning in CI (the dependency audit already blocks merges on high severity advisories).

1947.content: Postgres row level security as an extra isolation layer.

1948.content: An OpenTofu runner that does not need the Docker socket (ECS RunTask or a Kubernetes Job).

1949.content:
Email **security@orkstage.io** with the details and, if you can, a proof of concept. Please do not
open public issues for security problems. We acknowledge each report and coordinate disclosure with
you.

1951.content: Fixes for common OrkStage problems, from startup configuration errors and busy ports to MiniStack, OpenTofu runners, state buckets, permissions and webhooks.

1953.content:
Start with the **correlation id**. Every API error and every deployment carries one. Search the API
and worker logs for it.

1954.content:
OrkStage validates its configuration at startup and lists every problem, for example
`SESSION_SECRET: Too small: expected string to have >=32 characters` or `ENCRYPTION_KEY: Set ENCRYPTION_KEY (32 bytes, base64) in production.`
Fix the variables it names (see the configuration reference).

1955.content:
In production, OrkStage refuses on purpose to start with the dev login, private webhooks, a missing
`ENCRYPTION_KEY` or a session secret that starts with `change-me`.

1956.content:
The stack publishes ports `3000`, `4000`, `4566`, `5432`, `6379`, `1025` and `8025`. Stop the process
that holds the port (often a local Postgres or Redis), or change the left side of the port mapping in
`docker-compose.yml` in `orkstage-dev`. If you move `3000` or `4000`, update `WEB_PUBLIC_URL` or
`API_PUBLIC_URL` to match.

1957.content:
MiniStack needs the Docker socket (`/var/run/docker.sock`) to start real containers. On Docker
Desktop, enable the default socket. With rootless Docker or Podman, mount the matching socket path.

1958.content:
The containers MiniStack starts join the `orkstage_default` network. If you renamed the
Compose project, update `DOCKER_NETWORK` for MiniStack and `TOFU_DOCKER_NETWORK` for the worker.
Check the logs with `docker compose logs ministack`.

1959.content:
On real AWS, the state bucket must exist before the first deployment, with versioning and
encryption. Its name is `orkstage-tfstate-<account>-<region>`, or the name set in `stateBucket` on
the target.

1960.content:
On MiniStack, OrkStage creates the bucket on first use. A state bucket error there usually means the
emulator is not running or the endpoint is wrong (`endpointUrl` on the target, or
`AWS_EMULATOR_ENDPOINT`). See Connecting an AWS account.

1961.content:
The deployment role lacks actions that the deployed services need, and the event log names them.
Update the role from the current `infra/aws/orkstage-deployment-role.yaml`, then validate the target
again. If the check reports that it was skipped, the role is missing `iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy`
on itself.

1962.content:
The worker starts OpenTofu runners through the Docker socket, which is why it runs as root in
Compose. Check that:

1963.content: the socket is mounted into the worker;

1964.content:
the `TOFU_WORK_VOLUME` and `TOFU_PLUGIN_CACHE_VOLUME` volumes exist
(`docker volume ls | grep orkstage-tofu`);

1965.content:
the runner image is built
(`docker compose --profile platform build tofu-runner`).

1966.content: OrkStage kills a command that runs longer than `TOFU_TIMEOUT_MINUTES`.

1967.content:
Only one operation runs on an instance at a time. Wait for the current deployment to finish, or
cancel it, then deploy again. A deployment parked in `AWAITING_APPROVAL` also keeps the instance busy
until someone approves or cancels it.

1968.content:
Someone deleted the resource outside OrkStage. Deploy again, and OrkStage recreates the missing
resource.

1969.content:
Webhook URLs must use `https://` and resolve to public addresses. To test with a receiver on your own
machine, set `WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE=true` (development only), or use a tunnel with a public HTTPS URL.

1970.content:
The server does not have the WebAssembly scan engine installed. Scan on your machine with
`ork import` (Preview) and send the report, or install `@orkstage/scan` with the API.

1971.content:
The console reaches the API through its own origin. Check `API_INTERNAL_URL`, which is set when the
console is built, and check that the API answers `GET /api/v1/readyz`. Sessions expire after 12
hours, so you may only need to sign in again.

1973.content: Upgrade OrkStage on your own infrastructure. Rebuild images, apply Prisma migrations, update the OpenTofu runner and move instances to new template versions.

1976.content: Get the new code and rebuild

1982.content:
OrkStage has no tagged releases yet, so an upgrade means moving to a newer commit of the platform.
The procedure below is the one for the Docker Compose stack.

1983.content:
Take a database backup first (see Backups and recovery). Migrations
only move forward.

1984.content:
The `migrate` service runs `prisma migrate deploy`, which applies only pending migrations, then the
idempotent seed, and exits. The `api`, `worker` and `web` services start only after it succeeds. On
an installation without containers, run `pnpm db:deploy && pnpm db:seed` instead.

1985.content:
Deployments in progress survive a worker restart: BullMQ delivers the job again, and the deployment
resumes from its persisted steps. Even so, upgrade while no deployment is running when you can.

1986.content:
Migrations live in `packages/database/prisma/migrations`. Prisma generates them from
`schema.prisma` during development (`pnpm db:migrate`). The append only trigger on the audit table is
part of a migration, so never edit it by hand.

1987.content:
The runner image pins the OpenTofu version (`1.12.7`) and contains the modules. To upgrade them,
change `TOFU_IMAGE` on purpose, or rebuild `orkstage/tofu-runner:local`. The modules have their own
repository, `orkstage-modules`, with their own versions. Once its runner image is published, the
platform pins `TOFU_IMAGE=ghcr.io/orkstage/tofu-runner:vX.Y.Z`, and each change to infrastructure
code becomes a deliberate upgrade.

1988.content:
A module change alters the plan of existing resources. The next deployment of each instance shows
the change as a provider plan, and
destructive changes in production wait for approval.

1989.content:
Instances never move to a new template version on their own. Publish the new version, then use
**Upgrade template** on each instance, review the plan and deploy.

1990.content:
The template schema has a version (`apiVersion: platform/v1`). Changes to the API that break clients
will come with a new `/api/v2` route group. After the split, a compatibility matrix in `orkstage-dev`
will list the tested combination of platform, console, CLI and modules for each release.

1992.content: A tour of the OrkStage web console. How to sign in, what each role sees, the overview, instance tabs, deployments, incidents and the theme.

1999.content:
The console is a Next.js application served next to the API. It calls the API through its own
origin, so session cookies stay first party and no cross origin requests are needed.

2000.content:
**Single sign on**: every provider configured with OIDC appears on the login page. Microsoft Entra
ID is the reference provider, and you can add any other OIDC provider through configuration. See
Configuration.

2001.content:
**Development login**: an email only login for local installs. It is off unless
`AUTH_DEV_LOGIN_ENABLED=true`, and the API refuses to start with it on when
`NODE_ENV=production`.

2002.content: A session lasts 12 hours. Signing out revokes it.

2003.content:
The menu depends on your role. The console hides actions you cannot
perform, but the API checks every action again, so a hidden button is never the only protection.
